notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes for you.

My first batch of page requests failed with an error. When I tried to look into it, the tool told me I'd used up my allowed calls for this turn. That means I didn't read any of the pages: Enduring Word, the BibleHub/StudyLight commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Wesley's notes, Precept Austin or Augustine on New Advent. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I can't give you any verse notes for Psalm 10.

**Next step:** ask me again in a new turn and I'll start over. I'd fetch the pages one or two at a time so one failure doesn't stop the whole batch. I'd start with:
- enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-10/
- the BibleHub verse pages (biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/10-1.htm through 10-18.htm) for Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and others
- studylight.org for Wesley's notes and the Geneva Bible notes
- preceptaustin.org's Psalm 10 page
- netbible.org's translator notes
- newadvent.org for Augustine's comments. His Bible numbered the Psalms differently, so Psalm 10 is the second half of his "Psalm 9."

After that I'd search the tradition-specific sites (Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Seedbed, 1517, LCMS and others) for places where they really disagree. Then I'd write the notes verse by verse ("v. 4: ...") with a URL after each point and leave out anything I can't find.
